answer: Each agent identity must lease a "vine node" on a mesh of peer verifiers: the first identity costs 200 tokens, but each additional identity's bond is quadratic — identity n locks 200·(n−1)² tokens — while a proof-of-compute "pulse" (a signed benchmark replayed hourly) proves dedicated hardware, since CPU cycles can't be shared across identities. Slashing removes the whole knoll of linked bonds when any two nodes collude in double-attestation, making scale attacks prohibitively expensive.
